name: window.close
description: Send `WM_CLOSE` to the window. The window may decline (apps with unsaved work typically prompt the user instead of closing). The OK confirms the message was posted, not that the window closed.

x-output-schema.description: Empty body — wire response is the literal `OK 0`.

x-implementations.name: post_message_close
x-implementations.description: Win32 `PostMessage(hwnd, WM_CLOSE, 0, 0)`. Non-blocking; the window's wndproc decides whether to close, prompt, or ignore.

windows-modern.description: PostMessage WM_CLOSE. Subject to UIPI: posting to a higher-IL window from a lower-IL agent surfaces no error here (PostMessage returns success) but the message never delivers. Use system.info.integrity + uiaccess to assess reach before calling.

windows-classic.description: PostMessage WM_CLOSE. NT 4 / 9x / 2000: no UIPI, all messages deliver. NT 5+ behaves like windows-modern.
